chunks: Regarding a man who forgot the tashahhud in the salat (prayer), he said: “If he remembers that he said only ‘Bismillah,’ then his salat (prayer) is valid. But if he does not remember anything of the tashahhud, he must repeat the salat (prayer).”

And concerning a man who remembers after he has stood up, spoken, and gone about his needs, that he had only prayed two rak'ahs in the zuhr, 'asr, 'atamah, or maghrib, he said: “He continues on the basis of his salat (prayer) and completes it, even if he has reached China, and he does not repeat the salat (prayer).”

So this is not contrary to what we mentioned, that whoever speaks deliberately must repeat the salat (prayer), because one who forgets, gives salam, and then speaks afterward has not intentionally spoken while being in the salat (prayer). Rather, he only spoke because he thought that he had finished the salat (prayer), so he takes the ruling of one who was in the salat (prayer) yet spoke thinking that he was not in the salat (prayer).

But if, when he remembered that something from these salats (prayers) had been missed, he then spoke deliberately after that, it would be obligatory upon him to repeat the salat (prayer), in accordance with what we set forth regarding one who speaks deliberately.

And whoever doubts, not knowing whether he prayed two or three, then if his supposition inclines to one of them he builds upon it and nothing is due upon him. But if his supposition is balanced, he builds upon the greater number and completes what he missed after giving salam. We have already presented what indicates that, and what further clarifies it is what he narrated:

As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام: concerning—

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: the testimony recited in the sitting of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the ritual salat (prayer) being discussed in its legal rulings
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: gave the salutation ending the salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَهَا: forgot or erred unintentionally in salat (prayer)
key_terms.وَهْمُهُ: his presumptive inclination or stronger supposition

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets tashahhud or doubts the number of rak'ahs in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings of forgetfulness and doubt in salat (prayer), including forgetting the tashahhud, realizing that some rak'ahs were omitted after speaking, and uncertainty between the number of rak'ahs prayed. It distinguishes between deliberate speech during salat (prayer) and speech uttered under the assumption that the salat (prayer) had ended, and it lays out how one should proceed in completing the prayer.
